title: Continuous affinity scheduler for dialogue imbalance and KV safeguards
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads cause inefficient slot packing and KV cache churn. Short prompts + long responses or interleaved small/large turns create slot affinity thrashing and frequent KV evictions, which increases end-to-end latency and token cost.

Goal: Implement a continuous affinity scheduler that groups streams by 'dialogue imbalance score' and enforces KV safety lanes (soft reservations) to reduce eviction churn and GPU memory fragmentation while preserving tail latency SLOs. This ticket covers design, prototype, benchmark, and a staged rollout with telemetry and fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler groups >80% of high-imbalance streams into affinity lanes under load profile A during the 95th percentile latency test
KV eviction rate reduced by >=40% on mixed dialogue test harness compared to baseline continuous scheduler
No customer-facing error increase during canary rollout (errors <= baseline + 0.5%)
Integration tests for soft-preempt and safety-lane spillover pass in CI and on dedicated perf cluster
design_notes: Introduce Dialogue Imbalance Score (DIS): a lightweight per-stream metric computed from recent (N=10) turn length distribution: DIS = max(turn_length) / mean(turn_length+1). Higher DIS indicates large asymmetric responses following short prompts.

Affinity lanes: three lanes (steady, mixed, imbalance) where streams are routed by DIS with hysteresis to avoid flapping. Each lane has an adaptive slot reservation percentage tuned by utilization histograms.
KV safety lanes: soft reservations of KV residency (in MB) per lane. Safety reservations are elastic: they can be borrowed by low-priority lanes under strict preemption rules (soft-preempt tokens).

Slot soft-preempt: allow temporarily stealing a slot from steady lane to serve an imbalance lane request if latency budget permits; preemption is delayed until model prefix compute completes to avoid wasted KV warmups.
Prefetch gating: for imbalance lane long responses, gate aggressive prefetch to avoid prefetching tokens beyond a dynamic horizon when slab pressure is high.
Compaction points: schedule periodic GPU memory compaction (KV trimming) during low traffic windows identified by the runtime heatmap to reduce fragmentation.
Threshold annealing: safety-lane thresholds adjust over minutes based on rolling eviction and 95p latency to stabilize allocations during bursts.
rollout_plan: Bench prototype on perf cluster (W2): run mixed-dialogue harness (90% short prompts, 10% long responses) and steady throughput sweep
Internal canary: 1% production traffic, enable telemetry and auto-fallback after 10m if error/latency regressions (W3)
Gradual ramp to 10% then 50% over two weeks with A/B measurement against baseline scheduler (W4-W5)
Full rollout if metrics meet acceptance criteria; otherwise revert and iterate (W6)
telemetry_metrics: KV eviction count and bytes evicted per minute per lane
Slot churn rate: average slot reassignment frequency per stream
95p and 99p token-latency and end-to-end response latency by lane
Error rate and model failure reasons tied to preempt events
test_plan: Unit: DIS calculation edge cases, hysteresis transitions, slot soft-preempt state machine
Integration: end-to-end with kv cache enabled, simulate preemption and spillover, validate no double-warmups
Perf: compare throughput/latency and KV eviction vs baseline across three workload mixes (steady, skewed-imbalance, random interleaving)
Chaos: inject artificially high slab fragmentation and validate compaction scheduling doesn't violate latency SLOs
CI gating: regression tests for memory leaks and increased tail latency
comments: 2025-11-03 Maya Chen: Created ticket. Initial idea surfaced during weekly runtime sync; customer incidents showed repeated KV thrash for conversational assistant workload.
2025-11-04 Arjun Patel: Spike started to validate DIS heuristics locally. Early results show DIS separates streams with >2x eviction rate.
2025-11-06 QA: Added integration scenarios for preemption races. Noted potential double-warmup when preempt occurs mid-prefix - design updated to delay preempt until prefix compute finishes.

2025-11-08 Perf: Prototype run on perf cluster with mixed-dialogue profile: baseline eviction 12.4 MB/min, prototype 6.9 MB/min (~44% reduction). 95p latency improved by 8%. Need more runs at higher QPS.
2025-11-10 Design review: PM and SRE approved safety lanes but requested hard cap safeguard if GPU memory pressure exceeds 92% to avoid OOM. Added compaction trigger and emergency spill policy.
2025-11-12 Arjun Patel: Pushed prototype PR for internal review. Next: extend telemetry and schedule canary window.
